title: Protein Stabilization of Emulsions and Foams: Physical Chemistry Principles
findings_summary: Demonstrated that globular protein foaming capacity depends on rapid interfacial adsorption and partial unfolding (denaturation) at air-water interfaces, establishing viscoelastic cohesive 2D films through intermolecular disulfide bonds and hydrophobic interactions.

title: Food emulsions and foams: Stabilization by particles and hydrocolloids
findings_summary: Investigated synergistic stabilization of air bubbles by polysaccharides (xanthan, guar) through bulk continuous phase thickening, showing that increasing viscosity reduces gravitational Plateau border drainage by a factor of 10 to 50.

title: A study of the factors affecting the foaming properties of egg white: pH, temperature, and sucrose additions
findings_summary: Egg white overrun exceeded 650% with whipping time of 3 minutes. Addition of sucrose at early stages reduced initial overrun but increased foam drainage half-life from 18 minutes to over 120 minutes by elevating liquid viscosity.

journal: Current Opinion in Colloid & Interface Science
title: Mechanisms involved in the formation and stabilization of food foams
findings_summary: Identified the three primary thermodynamic instability drivers in culinary foams: drainage driven by gravity and Laplace capillary pressure in Plateau borders, bubble disproportionation via Ostwald ripening, and bubble coalescence through film rupture.

title: Instability and Partial Coalescence in Whippable Dairy Emulsions
findings_summary: Whipped heavy cream stability relies on partial coalescence of partially crystalline fat globules that bridge at the air-water interface to form a rigid 3D fat-crystal continuous network. Excess liquid oil or temperature above fat melting point causes complete foam collapse.

title: Composition and properties of aquafaba: Water extract from chickpea cooking and its culinary application
findings_summary: Aquafaba foaming properties are governed by soluble protein fractions (~1.5 wt%) and arabinogalactan polysaccharides that retard liquid drainage. Produces overrun of 400-500% with drainage stability comparable to egg white when stabilized with acid.
